messages:
elena: Ran into a weird hang while walking a new hire through the Go generator sample. If the auth token rotates mid-stream the app blocks on gen.Next() and never recovers.

tom: can you share the tiny repro and a stack? usually a recv goroutine waiting on a channel.

elena: repro flags: `./examples/generator --stream --rotate-auth=3s`. Logs show refresh/handshake retry then main stuck. Stack shows gen.recvLoop waiting on chan receive.

yasmin: UX issue: Next() is blocking with no way to pass a context. other SDKs let you cancel/interrupt pulls. This makes the sample brittle during onboarding.

sam: options: (A) add Next(ctx) and keep Next() as sugar, (B) make SDK auto-close iterator on fatal handshake, (C) document Close() workaround. I prefer A for parity and clarity.

yasmin: agreed. also add a sample flag like `--auth-verbose` to print refresh lifecycle so new users can see what happened. Silent retries confuse people.

tom: implementation notes: Next(ctx) should return ctx.Err() when cancelled, Close() must be safe to call concurrently and idempotent, and tests should simulate 401->refresh and assert goroutine counts return to baseline. Add a microbench to ensure no alloc regressions in the non-ctx path.

elena: short-term workaround: run Next() in a goroutine and call gen.Close() on ctx.Done(). Ugly but works. I'll attach minimal repro and a heap trace to the new issue.

ci-bot: created issue #11642: "go: generator sample hangs on auth rotation; add ctx-aware Next and auth verbose sample". Labels: devex, needs-repro.

sam: i'll draft a small RFC and prototype PR. ping here when ready and we'll run the perf tests and onboarding quickstart. Thanks all. :pray:
